# Wiki and help 3.0: rebuild design

Status: design, for review. Target: 3.0. Nothing here is built yet.

The wiki and the help that ships in the packages are made from the same text (`tools/wiki/text`, `tools/wiki/pages`) by
`tools/wiki/wiki.py`. [#703](https://github.com/Xaymar/BlitzLLVM/pull/703) replaces how the help looks (a static
HTML5 site with search, themes and a sidebar). This document is about the other half: what the pages are, how they
are grouped and what they say. It changes no renderer code that #703 changes, and lands after #703.

## What is wrong now

1. **"Features" is a catch-all.** The sidebar has three hand-made groups (Getting started, Language, Tools). Every
   other guide page is filed under Differences > Features only because it has an `@difference` line, so Physics,
   CPU optimizations, IPv6 and Colors sit in one alphabetical list of 25. Everything is a feature, so the name says
   nothing, and a reader looking for "how do I make it faster" or "what does BlitzLLVM add" has no place to look.
2. **Pages hold several topics.** CPU optimizations has CPU features, threads and the memory allocator; GPU
   optimizations has culling, the spatial grid, GPU-driven draws and sprite shapes; Quality improvements has the
   depth buffer, many lights, large meshes and mip maps. A topic has no page to link to, and new ones (normal packing,
   cache-aligned allocations) have nowhere to go.
3. **Shipped features have no page at all**: the renderers (Vulkan, Direct3D 11, OpenGL and `BLITZLLVM_RENDERER`),
   HDR and AutoHDR, order-independent transparency, anti-aliasing, dithering and deep color, normal maps, the frame
   rate limiter, stencil buffers and clip planes, audio effects, 3D sound falloff, input devices (hot-plug, raw
   input), `AsyncSaving`, normal packing, cache-aligned allocations, texture streaming, the `blitzcc` command line.
   They only appear on command pages or in the changelog.
4. **Language Features has gaps and misfiled pages.**
   - No page for `Dim`, Blitz arrays (`Local a[5]`, `Global`, `Field`), `Type`, `Field`, `New`, `Delete`, `Each`,
     `First`, `Last`, `Before`, `After`, `Insert`, `Null`, `True`, `False`, `Data`, `Read`, `Restore`, `And`, `Or`,
     `Not`, `Xor`, `Shl`, `Shr`, `Sar`, `Void`, `In`, `Out`, `InOut`. They are only described in the long Language
     page.
   - `EndType` is under Types (the number types) while `Type` itself has no page.
   - "Other" is a second catch-all: 11 `Profile*` commands next to `CallDLL`, `GetEnv`, `ExecFile` and `RuntimeError`.
5. **Examples break unnoticed.** On a pull request the Wiki workflow runs `wiki.py check` without a compiler; the
   examples are only compiled against the nightly after the merge. Right now 9 pages fail on root (TerrainY, Double,
   Long, SatInt, SatUInt, SatULong, Parameter-Modes, Types, blitz-format), mostly because literals above the Int
   range became 2147483647 without an `i64` suffix.
6. **Names and titles are mixed**: "Include Files" and "Language Quirks" in title case, everything else in sentence
   case; "Types and numbers" (page) next to "Types" (category); tool titles (fixed by #703).

## Sidebar and categories

The guide groups replace "Features". Every hand-written page names its group with one line under its heading,
`@group Optimizations`, instead of `wiki.py` keeping a list (the list in `GROUPS` keeps only the order of groups).
A page without `@group` fails `wiki.py check`, so nothing lands in a catch-all again. `@difference` stays: it still
fills the Differences page, but no longer decides where a page is listed. The Differences submenu keeps only
Overview and Commands.

Order in the sidebar (wiki and help):

| Group | Pages |
|---|---|
| Getting started | Installation, Building, Coming from Blitz3D and BlitzPlus (new: what to expect, links into Differences), Differences |
| Language | Language (overview, shortened), Types and numbers, Vectors and matrices, Arrays (new), Parameter modes, Include files, Userlib declarations, Language quirks, Modern mode (when #700/#715 land) |
| Graphics | Renderers (new), Colors, HDR and AutoHDR (new), Deep color and dithering (new), Anti-aliasing (new), Transparency and OIT (new), Soft edges (Sprite-Depth-Fade renamed, sprites and entities), Spherical fog, Normal maps (new), Lights and light channels (from Quality improvements), Depth buffer (from Quality improvements), Large meshes (from Quality improvements), Mip maps and texture filtering (from Quality improvements), Stencil and clip planes (new), Frame rate (new: `SetGraphicsRefreshRate`, `Flip`, VSync), Lost graphics device |
| Improvements | Asynchronous loading and saving (adds `AsyncSaving`), Image formats, Saving pictures, Model formats, Sound resampling, 3D sound falloff (new), Audio effects (new, with the 2.0 audio PRs), Movies (Movie controls renamed), Input devices (new) and Scan codes, Multiplayer, IPv6, Physics, Windows of BlitzPlus |
| Optimizations | Overview (new: what is on by default, what needs a change in the program, how to measure with Profiling) and one page each: CPU instruction sets, Threads, Main thread on the first core, Memory allocator, Cache-aligned allocations (new), Culling, Spatial grid, GPU-driven draws (`EntityStatic`), Sprite shapes, Normal packing (new, #653), Vertex format (with #654), Texture streaming (new, #478), Video memory defragmentation (new, #450/#477) |
| Tools | blitzcc (new: command line), blitz-format, blitz-tidy, blitz-recompiler, Warnings, Environment variables, Profiling, Debug handle checks |

Graphics is split out of Improvements because it alone would hold half of it; if you prefer only the two groups you
named, Graphics folds into Improvements unchanged.

Each Optimizations page has the same parts: what it does, whether the program has to change, how to turn it off
(environment variable or command), and measured numbers only from a physical machine, with the machine named.

## Language Features

| Category | Pages |
|---|---|
| Arrays (new) | `Dim`, Blitz arrays (page named `Blitz-Arrays`, no keyword of its own) |
| Custom types (new) | `Type`, `Field`, `EndType` (moved), `New`, `Delete`, `Each`, `First`, `Last`, `Before`, `After`, `Insert`, `Null` |
| Data (new) | `Data`, `Read`, `Restore` |
| Operators (new) | `And`, `Or`, `Not`, `Xor`, `Shl`, `Shr`, `Sar`, `Mod` (moved from Math), `True`, `False` |
| Functions | adds `Void`, `In`, `Out`, `InOut` |
| Profiling (new) | the 11 `Profile*` commands, moved out of Other |
| System (Other renamed) | `AppTitle`, `CallDLL`, `CommandLine`, `DebugLog`, `ExecFile`, `GetEnv`, `SetEnv`, `RuntimeError`, `RuntimeStats`, `SystemProperty` |

The Language page shrinks to an overview that links these pages instead of repeating them.

What the array pages will say, checked against the original compiler (`third_party/blitz3d/compiler`):

- `Dim name(n[, m ...])`: indices 0 to n, any number of dimensions, sizes can be any expression. The array is global
  even when `Dim` runs in a function, but the first `Dim` of a name has to be in the main program ("Array not found
  in main program"). Running `Dim` again with the same number of dimensions makes a new, empty array of the new
  size. A Dim array can not be passed to a function.
- `Local a[n]`, `Global a[n]`, `Field a[n]`: one dimension, indices 0 to n (so `n + 1` elements), the size must be a
  constant and not negative ("Blitz array sizes must be constant"). A constant index above the size is a compile
  error; any other index is checked only in debug builds ("Blitz array index out of bounds"). A local one is new and
  empty on every call; every object of a type gets its own. It can be a parameter (`Function f(a[3])`), which passes
  the array itself, so the function changes the caller's array; the sizes have to match. It can not be assigned
  (`a = b` is "Blitz arrays can not be assigned to"), returned or made `Const`.
- BlitzLLVM additions and differences to confirm with the compiler before writing: `Local a:FloatVector3[4]`,
  local arrays over 4 KiB on the heap (#349 warning), the `compatibility-blitz-array-suffix` warning.

## Checks

- `wiki.py check` fails for a hand-written page without `@group`, a group that is not in `GROUPS`, and a page in
  Language Features without `@syntax` or a command of the list.
- The Wiki workflow on a pull request builds `blitzcc` (or takes the one the Build workflow made for the same
  commit) and runs `wiki.py check --blitzcc`, so a compiler change that breaks an example fails the pull request
  that makes it, not root afterwards.
- The 9 examples failing on root get fixed first, in their own pull request.

## Order of work

One pull request per step, each small enough to review:

1. Fix the 9 failing examples (their own PR, before anything else).
2. Examples compiled on pull requests (Wiki workflow).
3. `@group` and the new sidebar groups, moving existing pages only (no new text). After #703.
4. Language Features: Arrays, Custom types, Data, Operators, Profiling, System.
5. Split CPU optimizations, GPU optimizations and Quality improvements into one page per topic.
6. New pages for the shipped features without one, a few per PR, grouped by area.
7. Shorten Language and Home to overviews that link the new pages.

## Open questions

1. Graphics as its own group, or folded into Improvements?
2. Is "Coming from Blitz3D and BlitzPlus" wanted, or is Differences enough?
3. Should steps 1 and 2 (failing examples, examples on PRs) go ahead now, before 3.0?
